tokyo_kanmi_mitsuya.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop has a bilingual first-party site and it is deliberately minimal: hours (12:00–17:00, last orders 16:30, 完売次第終了 — closing when sold out), the address 台東区浅草1-32-13, a phone number, and the instruction 「お問い合わせはインスタグラムのメッセージからお願いします」 — enquiries by Instagram message. A /menu/ path returns 404. There is no board published anywhere on the site. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WORTH A RE-CHECK RATHER THAN A SHRUG, BECAUSE OF WHAT IT IS. 甘味 shops are the best dessert format in Japan for both diets — the 甘味処 西山 record elsewhere in this set shows why: 寒天 (agar, from seaweed), あんこ (azuki and sugar), 白玉 (glutinous RICE flour) and 黒蜜 are all plant and all wheat-free, so anmitsu, mamekan and zenzai are routinely safe on both counts where nothing else on a Japanese menu is. A kanmi counter that sells out daily is exactly the kind of place worth the phone call. But nothing about THIS shop’s bowls is published, and the general shape of the category is not evidence about this kitchen — so no items are recorded. Ask on Instagram, or re-check when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_tsukemen_gonokami_seisak.price_note: Complete card from the operator’s own page for this specific branch (株式会社五ノ神製作所 keeps one page per shop; this is 新宿, 渋谷区千駄ヶ谷5-33-16, 11:00-21:30 with last order 21:00, open daily). The shop describes itself as an 海老つけ麺専門店 — a prawn-tsukemen specialist — and says the Shinjuku bowls push the prawn flavour harder than the 本店 does. Bilingual JP/EN names as printed. ⚠ TSUKEMEN IS THE WORST-CASE STRUCTURE FOR A COELIAC AND THIS SHOP ADDS A SECOND PROBLEM ON TOP. The noodle is wheat; the dipping broth is a reduced prawn-shell soup which in this genre is finished with soy tare; and 海老 (prawn) is itself one of Japan’s eight major allergens, so this is a shop a shellfish-allergic diner should skip entirely rather than negotiate. No allergen statement is published. ⚠ THE SIDE DISHES ARE NOT AN ESCAPE ROUTE: ご飯 at 150 yen is plain rice, but the 海老味たまごかけご飯 is TKG built on the same prawn tare, バジルご飯 carries a basil sauce of unpublished composition, and 焼チーズ飯 is grilled cheese. The toppings 味玉 and 三角メンマ are both soy-marinated, and チャーシュー is soy-braised. The only two items on this card with no obvious wheat route are the heaped cabbage and the mozzarella.

tokyo_bistro_coloris.price_note: Complete lunch and dinner course pricing from the shop’s own pages (Bistro COLORIS, since 2006, 新宿区西新宿7-16-1 第3歯朶ビル1F, tel 03-5389-1441, closed Sundays and public holidays except for booked parties). This is a course-only French bistro: NOT ONE À-LA-CARTE DISH IS PUBLISHED, only the course skeletons — 前菜 / スープ / 魚料理 / 肉料理 / パン2個 / デザート / 珈琲 or 紅茶 — so no individual dish name or diet flag can honestly be recorded. What is recorded is every course and its price, plus the à-la-carte supplements, which are the only single items the shop prices. ⚠ EVERY COURSE ON BOTH CARDS INCLUDES パン2個 AS A FIXED COMPONENT — two bread rolls are built into the price, not offered — so wheat is on the table by default at every seat, and the supplements list 自家製パン at 150 yen a piece and butter at 75 yen, confirming the bread is house-baked. A French bistro kitchen is a roux, flour-dusting and beurre-manié kitchen; nothing here is published about allergens, and the fish and meat dishes are 本日の (chef’s daily choice) so they cannot be checked ahead. ⚠ THE SITE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON LUNCH HOURS: the lunch MENU page heads the card 11:30～14:30 (L.o.12:30) while the shop-information block on the same page says ランチ 11:30～15:00 (14:00 L.o). Both are recorded as printed; ring to confirm. Dinner is 17:30-22:30 (21:30 L.o) per the info block and 17:30-21:30 (L.o.20:00) per the dinner card. The DINNER B+ course lets you choose one main from 6-10 dishes; DINNER C and above let you choose the meat.
